A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CFGM research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including the image-based prompts and trajectories.

before.justification: v1 reports original CFGM benchmark results, component ablations, model comparisons, transfer experiments and example trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a combined-baseline comparison and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The three CFGM components, Algorithms 1–3 and Appendix C prompts retain the same procedures. The added ExpeL + QuBE comparator and expanded explanations do not modify CFGM.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AlfWorld, WebShop and ScienceWorld, with WebShop-to-WebArena-Shopping transfer. The new efficiency analysis uses the existing AlfWorld setting and introduces no additional task or environment coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ExpeL + QuBE as a combined offline-experience and online-reflection comparator across the three main benchmarks. ReAct, ExpeL, AutoGuide and QuBE remain; comparator membership in the existing supplementary comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new efficiency evaluation measures offline tokens per training sample, online tokens per step and interaction turns per trajectory (v2 Table 6). Existing accuracy metrics, model configurations, splits and task budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an AlfWorld efficiency analysis examining resource consumption and interaction length. Existing component, retrieval-scope, model-generalization, transfer and reflection analyses, together with Appendix D case studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same four-fold validation and mean/standard-error reporting statement. The added Table 1 comparator follows the existing uncertainty format; no new seeds, run-count disclosures, confidence intervals or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds ExpeL + QuBE results: 85.07% AlfWorld SR, 75.6 WebShop reward and 49% SR, and 65% ScienceWorld SR. New Table 6 reports efficiency results, including CFGM's 4068.5 offline tokens/sample, 4681.4 online tokens/step and 14.32 turns/trajectory. Previously reported scores and Figure 3 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical content, including Appendix A's WebShop reward equations, is unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new synergy discussion adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about coarse-to-fine memory grounding, superior benchmark performance and component effectiveness. The introduction's added offline/online wording clarifies existing claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets the combined-baseline comparison as evidence of integrated, '1+1>2' synergy beyond simply combining existing techniques. Section 4.3 links fewer interaction turns to potentially lower latency and cost. The limitations concerning small training sets and long retrieved trajectories remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table 6 discloses resource-use estimates for offline processing and online inference. This is limited additional cost information: model identifiers, retrieval parameters, task limits and prompt templates remain unchanged, and the appendix parameter table is merely renumbered from Table 6 to Table 7.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including MSI-agent, Amulet, retrieval-augmented hierarchical reinforcement learning and reinforcement-learning background works. It also explicitly distinguishes CFGM from a simple combination of existing techniques. The related-work organization remains intact; merging duplicate Reflexion references does not remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical corrections, clarifies offline/online terminology, expands the results discussion and adds acknowledgments. The section hierarchy and most existing prose, including the appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a comparator row and revised second-best highlighting, and a new efficiency table appears. Figure 2 has small schematic revisions, Figure 1's caption is clarified, and Figure 3 moves to the next page. Appendix figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The ExpeL + QuBE control strengthens the comparative evidence, while Table 6 supplies previously absent information about computational costs. These are useful but limited gains. The combined baseline lacks detailed implementation documentation, and its results do not by themselves establish the newly asserted superadditive synergy. The method, earlier results and principal reproducibility details otherwise remain stable.
